title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Atlas Finance
summary: POC scoping call to decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is sizing workloads (qps, tokens per request), defining success criteria (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost targets, data residency), and agreeing on benchmarks and a 4-week POC plan. Main concerns: latency, predictable throughput, SOC2/audit logs, SAML SSO, encryption/KMS, and cost per token. Next steps: share pricing and benchmark template, run initial integration, schedule week-by-week milestones.
next_steps: Alex to send pricing sheet + hosted/dedicated/private cost comparison (incl. reserved capacity options) - by 2026-06-03
Samir to share benchmark template and example scripts + runbook for integration tests - by 2026-06-02
Atlas to provide sample traffic profile (qps, avg tokens, peak windows) and 3 representative prompts - by 2026-06-01
Schedule technical benchmark call (week 2) after initial infra is connected - propose 2026-06-10
action_items: Alex Reyes - Send pricing + committed capacity options and example SLOs - due 2026-06-03
Samir Patel - Share benchmark harness (JMeter scripts, tokenization examples) and run initial smoke tests on hosted - due 2026-06-02
Jordan Li - Provide 3 canonical prompts, traffic histogram (last 30 days), and SLO targets - due 2026-06-01
Priya Singh - Share security contacts and required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, any regional data-residency reqs) - due 2026-06-04
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jordan (Atlas Head of ML), Priya (Atlas SRE), Markus (CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Alex, account lead for Redwood inference, with Samir our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Jordan: Yeah, hi, Jordan here. we run inference for transaction risk scoring and customer support triage at Atlas Finance. thanks for making time.
[00:14] Samir: Great to meet you. do you want to kick off with the current stack and the reason for the POC?
[00:20] Jordan: Sure. currently we have a hybrid setup - some on-prem GPUs for low-latency scoring, and we call OpenAI for longer form stuff. main pain points: unpredictable latency on external calls, high cost at scale, and data residency for EU customers. we want to evaluate Redwood for predictable inference - figure out whether hosted is enough or if we need dedicated or private.
[00:38] Markus: And importantly from infra side, we need predictable throughput during end-of-day batch runs and sub-200ms p50 for real-time scoring. p95 we want under 350ms ideally.
[00:47] Alex: Perfect. that's the exact scoping we aim to capture. quick qual questions: what's your steady-state qps and peak? tokens per request? typical sequence length?
[00:56] Jordan: steady qps about 120 reqs/s for scoring, peaks up to 450 during batch windows. avg tokens per request is around 320 tokens, 95th at ~900 for some longer customer-support contexts.
[01:08] Priya: Our SRE questions: do you support SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integrations? and can we run in our VPC?
[01:16] Samir: Yeah, Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem and KMS/HSM integrations. we also have enterprise options for SSO and audit logs; Hosted has SOC2 and configurable retention but if you need full control over keys and network isolation, Dedicated or Private is the typical path.
[01:28] Jordan: Any ballpark on cost per 1M tokens hosted vs dedicated? we've been getting quotes that hosted is cheaper to start but dedicated amortizes down if you commit.
[01:36] Alex: Exactly. hosted is lower up-front and easier to spin up for a POC. dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost when you have sustained load and reserved capacity. private has higher upfront for private control and on-prem infra. i'll send a comparative sheet after cal.
[01:48] Markus: For our POC success criteria, we're thinking: end-to-end latency p50 <200ms, p95 <350ms at 120 qps steady; throughput validation to show we can absorb 450 peak with autoscaling or burst; and cost estimate per 1M tokens under $X (we have internal target but will share).
[02:02] Jordan: also data handling: we cannot send EU customer data to non-EU regions; data residency and auditability are must-haves.
[02:09] Samir: Noted. we have region pinning and can run private deployments or dedicated in EU regions. for hosted we can route to EU-only infra and provide audit logs.
[02:18] Alex: ok let's map benchmarks. week 1: integration and smoke tests on hosted; week 2: run canonical benchmarks (latency/throughput) with your traffic generator; week 3: scale tests on dedicated nodes if you want to test reserved capacity; week 4: regression checks and runbook handover. Does that timeline work?
[02:35] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. we prefer a 4-week pilot. what about benchmark specifics? Samir, can you walk through what you'll measure?
[02:42] Samir: Sure. we'll measure p50/p90/p95 latencies for cold and warm starts, throughput at target qps, token throughput (tokens/s), and memory/GPU utilization. we'll also test prefix/KV cache impact on repeated prompts - we often see repeated prefixes in support threads.
[02:57] Priya: small note - we use KV cache term internally but some folks write it as K-V cash in docs, so watch for that in automation.
[03:03] Samir: ha, noted. we'll include a cache-aware workload. also we'll run experiments with quantized model variants; our runtime supports int8 paths which could reduce cost but slightly change quality.
[03:13] Jordan: how do we validate quality regressions when we change quantization or model variants? we need automatic evals against our prompt set.
[03:20] Samir: we can hook Redwood Optimize and our eval harness to run a prompt set and compute regression thresholds. we'll capture BLEU-ish or task-specific metrics; you can set quality SLOs so we never degrade beyond a threshold.
[03:31] Markus: network topology question, if we do dedicated in a cloud region how do fallbacks work if a zone has issues?
[03:37] Alex: we have smart routing \u2014 can route to another zone or fallback to hosted-compatible variants. for dedicated, we recommend a standby fallback configured in routing policy so traffic keeps flowing with a slightly higher latency but preserved availability.
[03:49] Jordan: ok. other constraints: we need SOC2 compliance, encryption at rest, and tenants separated. do you support per-tenant RBAC and token-level tracing?
[03:58] Samir: Yes, RBAC, per-token tracing in the console (cost + latency breakdown), and audit logs for enterprise.
[04:05] Priya: example failure modes \u2014 what happens to KV cache on autoscale, do you have cache warm-up strategies?
[04:11] Samir: autoscaling will spin up new nodes; KV caches are per-node so we rely on prefix caching and smart routing to direct warm requests to warmed nodes. we also support proactive pre-warming scripts in the runbook.
[04:23] Jordan: benchmark numbers we want to see: p50 <200ms, p95 <350ms at steady qps 120; and a test where we hit 450 for 5 minutes to validate scaling and fallbacks. also a cost-per-token estimate for 3 models: base open model, quantized variant, and a Redwood-verified low-latency model.
[04:40] Alex: we'll prepare a benchmark plan with those exact scenarios. Samir will provide the harness and config. for POC scope, we recommend starting on Hosted for week 1 to validate integration and latency quickly; if results show we need consistent lower unit cost and reserved throughput we spin up Dedicated in week 3; Private is reserved for customers who need on-premised or strict data residency.
[04:58] Markus: What's the lift to try hosted first then move to dedicated mid-POC? how seamless is the pin/rollout?
[05:04] Samir: We've built the deployment abstraction so the API calls remain identical; you'd change routing and model version pins. there is some infra provisioning for dedicated (typically a few days for reserved capacity), but functionally it's a few config flips. we'll document it in the runbook.
[05:15] Jordan: Any red flags if we have long sequences (900 tokens) \u2014 will latency blow up?
[05:20] Samir: latency grows with sequence length but our kernels and KV cache optimizations help. we'll run the 900-token cases in benchmarks; if you need lower p95 at that length, Dedicated with larger GPU instances or model quantization can help.
[05:33] Priya: security review \u2014 do you provide VPC peering and private link?
[05:37] Alex: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering/PrivateLink. Hosted can use private endpoints for enterprise customers.
[05:45] Jordan: ok great. procurement aside, what would we need to sign to start a POC? is there a POC contract or just an MSA?
[05:51] Alex: usually for a 4-week POC we sign a simple POC SOW that outlines scope, success criteria, and trial credits. if you want Dedicated reserved capacity for the POC we include a short-term commitment. procurement can handle that in parallel.
[06:03] Markus: timeline check \u2014 if we start next week, can you have hosted ready in 3 business days?
[06:08] Samir: yes, hosted integration is typically <72 hours for API keys and test infra. Dedicated provisioning takes longer \u2014 usually 3-7 business days depending on region and GPU availability.
[06:18] Jordan: ok let's do hosted first. we'll provide sample prompts and traffic histograms by 6/1. schedule the week-2 benchmark deep-dive on 6/10.
[06:27] Alex: Perfect. i'll send pricing + the POC SOW and the benchmark template after this call. Samir will send the harness and run the initial smoke.
[06:34] Priya: last Q \u2014 are there any known differences in the hosted model catalog vs dedicated/private? same model versions?
[06:38] Samir: generally same model variants; dedicated/private can pin specific model versions and include custom quantization/artifacts if you bring your own model. hosted exposes our curated catalog and Redwood-verified performance profiles.
[06:49] Jordan: good. anything else?
[06:51] Alex: quick recap \u2014 deliverables: pricing sheet, POC SOW, benchmark template, harness, runbook. action items and due dates as we discussed. next meeting: benchmark deep-dive 2026-06-10.
[06:59] Markus: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:02] Jordan: thanks folks. bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings ("K-V cash" noted) and some speaker label drift early in the call. references: shared deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/atlas-poc), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/atlas-template), security docs (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2).
